stories.headline: Pakistan announces Islamabad meeting of ECO Council of Ministers for 15–16 November
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office announced on 14 November that Islamabad would host the 30th Economic Cooperation Organization Council of Ministers meeting on 15–16 November 2026. The gathering is scheduled, not yet completed; Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar is expected to chair it.
stories.background: ECO is a regional intergovernmental organisation focused on economic connectivity, trade and cooperation. Pakistan holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026–27.
stories.why_it_matters: The ministerial agenda offers a platform for regional connectivity and trade diplomacy, but planned discussions should not be mistaken for adopted agreements.
stories.pakistan_perspective: The announced theme, 'Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO', reflects Pakistan's stated regional-cooperation priorities.
key_takeaways: The 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting was announced for Islamabad on 15–16 November 2026.
quick_gk: Pakistan announced that Islamabad would host the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on 15–16 November 2026.
question_angles: Which city was announced on 14 November as host of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting?

sources.title: Pakistan to host 30th ECO Council of Ministers meeting on Nov 15-16

stories.headline: UN climate chief urges COP31 negotiators to accelerate talks amid fossil-fuel divisions
stories.summary: Reuters reported on 14 November that UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged COP31 negotiators in Antalya, Türkiye, to move quickly on difficult issues and avoid tactical delays. Disagreements over fossil-fuel language and climate finance remained unresolved; no final agreement was reported.
stories.background: COP31 negotiations address implementation of international climate commitments, adaptation finance and the transition away from fossil fuels.
stories.why_it_matters: Disputes over fossil-fuel wording and finance affect the credibility and implementation of international climate cooperation.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan's climate vulnerability makes adaptation funding and clarity on actual financial commitments especially important.
key_takeaways: Simon Stiell urged faster negotiations at COP31 on 14 November; the final outcome remained pending.
quick_gk: UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged COP31 delegates in Antalya to accelerate negotiations on 14 November 2026.
question_angles: Who urged COP31 negotiators to avoid tactical delays on 14 November 2026?

sources.title: UN climate chief urges speed as COP31 confronts fossil fuel divide

stories.headline: India sets out ambition to reach 900 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2035
stories.summary: Associated Press reported on 14 November that India aims to raise non-fossil electricity capacity to 900 gigawatts by 2035, from a little over 300 GW. Transmission, storage and rising demand remain significant constraints; the target is not capacity already installed.
stories.background: Installed renewable capacity and electricity actually delivered differ because grid congestion, storage limitations and generation profiles affect usable output.
stories.why_it_matters: India's plan illustrates the scale of investment needed to expand low-carbon power while maintaining grid reliability.
stories.pakistan_perspective: Pakistan faces related questions around grid investment, renewable integration, power-sector affordability and energy-import dependence.
key_takeaways: India's reported non-fossil electricity capacity ambition is 900 GW by 2035.
quick_gk: India aims for 900 GW of non-fossil electricity capacity by 2035, according to AP reporting on 14 November 2026.
question_angles: What non-fossil power capacity target for 2035 did India outline in November 2026?

sources.title: India seeks to triple clean energy capacity to 900 gigawatts by 2035, but major hurdles remain
